newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Superconductor to review proposal.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Superconductor to review proposal.

text.p: Illinois Superconductor Corp said Tuesday its board would review a major shareholder's proposal calling for the ouster of Chief Executive Officer Ora Smith and but one of the company's directors.

According to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, shareholder Sheldon Drobny, who owns a 7.7 percent stake in the company, has proposed all current board members except Smith resign. He has also proposed that all board members be significant stockholders.
Drobny also recommended that Smith be replaced as CEO, president and chairman by Semir Sirazi, currently vice president and general manager of 3Com Corp's Cable Access Business Unit.
Illinois Superconductor called the proposal a "road map" for taking control of the company.

In the filing, Drobny proposed replacing the board with Shan Padda, Stewart Shiman and Sirazi. He also called for an amendment to the shareholder rights plan to exclude common stock owned by Drobny, Shiman and Aaron Fischer.
"This would allow Mr. Drobny to gain control of the company without paying a premium to its other stockholders," Illinois Supercomputer said in a statement.
In his filing, Drobny called for the proposed new board to analyze Illinois Superconductor's financing agreements and make appropriate changes.
The company said on June 10 that it had secured a $15 million financing facility. It previously withdrew a one-million-share offering.
Illinois Superconductor said Drobny owes the company $140,387, excluding interest, and that an entity controlled by Drobny has guaranteed a loan of $558,120 by the company to other shareholders.
Both loans were extended by the company in November 1996 to fund stock purchases related to a private placement in November 1995. Both loans were originally due April 30, 1997.
The company said Drobny had not indicated what action the new directors would take with respect to the loans.
Drobny could not be reached for comment on the company's statement, but on Monday he called his proposal for a new board and CEO "friendly."
Drobny, who said he met with Smith last week, said it was time for the company to switch to a marketing mindset from a developmental focus.
"Depending on the board's response, we would like to have an orderly transition to move forward this week," Drobny said.
He said he had no doubts about Illinois Superconductor technology, but the company has failed to communicate its successes to the marketplace and the public.
The company said it has disclosed the names of its customers except when contracts include confidentiality agreements.
"The company intends to continue actively disclosing information to its stockholders and keeping them up to date about the company's business," Illinois Superconductor said.
